                    ### Question
                    A 58-year-old lifeguard develops squamous cell carcinoma of the skin on his forehead. Which of the following most likely preceded the development of this carcinoma?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Hamartomatous lesion of sebaceous glands
opb. Dry, scaly, hyperkeratotic papule
opc. A single, large pink patch
opd. Dermatophyte infection
ope. UVC exposure

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
UVC exposure is a known risk factor for squamous cell carcinoma development. Actinic keratosis, a dry, scaly, hyperkeratotic papule, is a precursor lesion to squamous cell carcinoma. Dermatophyte infection leading to chronic inflammation is not a direct precursor to squamous cell carcinoma. The most likely preceding condition in this case is the presence of actinic keratosis.
